goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes/updates the WorkflowReminder DB row, leaking rows that are never marked cancelled and never cleaned up until their scheduledDate naturally passes

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` returns early when `immediateDelete` is true after cancelling the SendGrid scheduled send (POST cancel), and it does not `delete` the `WorkflowReminder` row nor `update` it to `cancelled=true`. The only DB mutation in that branch is none. Meanwhile, the new cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only selects reminders with `cancelled: true` to cancel/delete them. Therefore any call sites passing `immediateDelete=true` (e.g. `workflowsRouter` when deleting a workflow/step, and `handleNewBooking` for rescheduled bookings) will leave DB rows behind that are neither deleted nor marked cancelled, and thus won't be picked up by the new cleanup logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/schema.prisma:644 — cancelled Boolean?` optional field has no application-level default or backfill, so old rows are ambiguous (NULL) vs new rows explicitly false/true

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `cancelled Boolean?` to `WorkflowReminder` and the migration simply `ADD COLUMN "cancelled" BOOLEAN;` with no default/backfill, so pre-existing rows will be NULL and new rows can also be NULL unless explicitly set. The new logic queries `cancelled: true` (e.g., `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`) and sets `cancelled: true` (in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`), but nothing in the diff enforces a consistent non-null false state for “not cancelled”, creating a tri-state (NULL/false/true) that can be confusing or error-prone if future code filters on `cancelled: false`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:46 — Query filters `cancelled: true`; safe against NULL today, but any future negation-style filter (`cancelled: false` or `{ not: true }`) would silently exclude all pre-migration NULL rows since no backfill set them to false

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a nullable `cancelled Boolean?` column (schema.prisma) with a migration that does not set a default or backfill existing rows (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN "cancelled" BOOLEAN;`). In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` the new query filters `cancelled: true`, which will work regardless of existing NULLs. The finding is not a present defect in this diff, but it correctly highlights a diff-created data-state risk: pre-migration rows will have `cancelled = NULL`, and any later code that uses negation-style filters like `cancelled: false` / `{ not: true }` would exclude those NULL rows unless the column is made non-null with a default/backfill.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder`'s optional `immediateDelete` boolean silently switches between hard-cancel-via-SendGrid (no DB update) and soft-cancel (sets `cancelled: true`, DB row untouched) with no doc comment, so call sites pass `true`/omit it inconsistently (handleNewBooking.ts:967, workflows.tsx:216, workflows.tsx:519) without any rationale for why that specific call needs immediate deletion

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` now has two materially different behaviors based on the optional `immediateDelete`: when `immediateDelete` is truthy it cancels via SendGrid and `return`s without updating/deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row; otherwise it only sets `cancelled: true` in DB (and does not cancel SendGrid immediately). Multiple call sites in the diff pass `true` (e.g., `handleNewBooking.ts` around the new cancellation block, and `workflows.tsx` in the deleted-workflow / deleted-step paths) while other call sites omit it, but there’s no inline explanation in the diff of why some paths require immediate hard-cancel vs soft-cancel. This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/clarity concern rather than a clearly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:210 — When `immediateDelete` is true and `referenceId` exists, the function cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or marking the WorkflowReminder row, leaving a stale "scheduled" reminder row in the DB that no other code path cleans up

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)`, when `referenceId` is non-null and `immediateDelete` is true, the function only posts a SendGrid cancel request and then `return`s without updating or deleting the corresponding `WorkflowReminder` row (`emailReminderManager.ts` new logic). Call sites in the diff pass `immediateDelete=true` (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` for rescheduled bookings, and `workflows.tsx` when deleting workflows/steps), so the DB row is left intact and not marked `cancelled`, meaning the new cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` (which only targets `cancelled: true`) will not remove it. This leaves stale reminder rows in the DB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/schema.prisma:644 — New nullable `cancelled Boolean?` field with no default overlaps in meaning with the existing `scheduled Boolean`, creating two independent boolean flags on WorkflowReminder instead of a single status enum (e.g. SCHEDULED/CANCELLED/SENT), risking inconsistent states like scheduled=true + cancelled=true

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `cancelled Boolean?` alongside existing `scheduled Boolean` on `WorkflowReminder` (schema.prisma). The new logic explicitly sets `cancelled: true` without changing `scheduled` (e.g., `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now does `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })` when `immediateDelete` is not set), which makes states like `scheduled=true` + `cancelled=true` possible. That state is used as a “pending cancellation” marker (see `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` querying `cancelled: true` to cancel and then delete), so it’s not a directly verifiable defect, but it does create two independent flags with overlapping lifecycle semantics and potential for misuse/inconsistent interpretation elsewhere in the codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177 — deleteScheduledSMSReminder` now hard-deletes the WorkflowReminder row unconditionally while the email equivalent sometimes soft-cancels and sometimes hard-deletes and sometimes leaves the row untouched, giving inconsistent semantics between the two reminder managers despite the near-identical call sites

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent and potentially broken DB cleanup semantics between reminder managers. `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` now always deletes the `workflowReminder` row (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)`) regardless of whether `referenceId` exists. In contrast, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` (a) deletes the row only when `referenceId` is null, (b) when `immediateDelete` is true it cancels the remote send and then `return`s without updating or deleting the DB row, and (c) otherwise only sets `cancelled: true`. Call sites were updated to use both forms (e.g. `handleNewBooking` passes `true` for rescheduled bookings), so email reminders can be left in the DB untouched while SMS reminders are removed, which is the inconsistency described and can lead to orphaned email reminder rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:317 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder signature changed (reminderId, nullable referenceId, immediateDelete flag) with three divergent code paths (delete/immediate-cancel/mark-cancelled) and no test exercises any branch

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` from a single-arg API to `(reminderId, referenceId|null, immediateDelete?)` and adds three distinct behaviors: hard DB delete when `referenceId` is null, immediate remote cancel when `immediateDelete` is true, or `cancelled: true` mark otherwise (`emailReminderManager.ts`). This is nontrivial control flow and several call sites were updated to pass the new args. The diff does not add or modify any tests to cover these new branches, but the specific claim that "no test exercises any branch" cannot be conclusively verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:124 — New cron logic that queries `cancelled: true` reminders, cancels via Sendgrid, and deletes them in a loop is entirely untested, including partial-failure behavior when client.request throws mid-loop leaving some reminders cancelled-in-provider but not deleted from DB

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new cancellation+deletion logic in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` that wraps the entire loop in a single `try/catch`. Because it does `await client.request(...)` inside the loop and only performs DB deletes later via `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`, any exception mid-loop will skip `Promise.all`, leaving already-cancelled Sendgrid sends (from earlier iterations) not deleted in Prisma. That partial-failure/inconsistent-state risk is diff-grounded. However, the claim that this is “entirely untested” is not verifiable from the diff alone (no test context shown).
